ac:layout-cell.p: Logical Feature Specification · API Reference · Sequence and Reuse Assessment · Feature landing page

This separate companion set reorganises SPEC-SEI-007 for stakeholder, business-process and engineering review. It assesses the supplied FR guide and preserved Send e-invoice OpenAPI snapshot. This revision records the proposed Spain onboarding handoff, six-case public-route rule, private-platform SPFE copy assumption, identity purposes, es.nif proposal and open withdrawal assessment. It retains the predecessor and existing OUT meanings. The OpenAPI snapshot documents the France-oriented contract; it does not prove Spain support or deployment.

ERP issuance ownership and independent action outcomes remain unchanged. The current journey sends one invoice for a business or its authorised accountant. PRD-SEI-246 records the local-product transitional PDF responsibility. The exact PDF channel and the coordination between issuance and copy remain open. SPEC-SEI-022 is selected for the existing Confluence page 923861395. The logical specification and sequence/reuse assessment are companion pages under the same feature. Publication is authorised; all three lifecycle statuses remain draft.

A Spanish business or authorised accountant must send an invoice or select a permitted correction or cancellation action for an issued invoice. The ERP owns issuance. The product must show each action's result and who must act next.

This summary is for Product, directors and cross-functional stakeholders. SPEC-SEI-023 owns the proposed behaviour in this set. SPEC-SEI-024 assesses existing APIs and evidence gaps. SPEC-SEI-043 owns the API reference. REF-BASE; REF-PRODUCT.

Use the shared glossary. The represented business, authenticated caller, invoice seller/buyer, approver and signer are distinct roles. Login, connection and certificate possession do not by themselves establish action authority.

An exchange action has one purpose and result, such as recipient delivery or faithful public-copy submission. A processing notification or technical acknowledgement does not establish buyer acceptance.

tr.td: Tax identity

The seller's NIF and the buyer's NIF or NIE identify invoice parties for tax purposes. An NIE is a NIF class for a foreign natural person, not a separate scheme. PRD-SEI-101, “Seller NIF vs Buyer NIF/NIE”.
Routing address

Identifies a network participant or destination. A NIF is a routing-address value only when the selected network contract defines a scheme such as es.nif; tax identity alone does not establish that mapping.
Certificate or signature
Any certificate or signature required for the selected action is a separate trust and authority concern. Certificate possession does not establish action authority.

ac:layout-cell.p: A configured sender access point is a sender connection available for qualification and per-invoice selection; a public recipient route is the destination selected under Spain recipient-routing rules. These are separate choices.

tr.td: Direct business or accountant for one client
Prepare, approve where authorised and send one invoice with current business/action authority.
Service-assisted draft entry and validation — TBC
Confirm scope and handoff. The proposed path returns issues before issuance; correction creates a new draft revision.
Final candidate ready
Qualify its exact data, recipient route, files, authority and required actions before dependent issuance.
Public or private recipient route
Select one eligible delivery route from current evidence. Apply Spain copy rules separately.
Explicit per-invoice selection

Proposed: Choose any one of the sender's ready, permitted connections for each invoice, including different private platforms on different invoices. The selected sender platform must support the recipient destination under SPEC-SEI-023 OUT-10. No fan-out or saved onboarding changes.
Sender connection and recipient destination differ
Keep the selected sender connection separate from the recipient destination and qualify both in the frozen plan.
Already-issued invoice or uncertain action
Preserve issuance and earlier results. Use the applicable correction or reconciliation path.
Transitional PDF required
The local product generates the matching PDF. Recipient delivery uses a separately qualified capability and owner. See OUT-PDF-R01/02.

ac:layout-cell.p: An accountant sending one client's invoice uses the same route and copy controls as the business user. Batch sending is not a prerequisite, and the supplied FR guide does not establish a bulk accountant requirement. Wider portfolio and accounting-handoff proposals stay separate under OUT-Q02.

Full setup belongs to onboarding. Creation, trust, route qualification and later lifecycle reporting retain their owning specifications. This sending set coordinates their handoffs; it does not approve new service boundaries. REF-BASE; REF-PRODUCT.

The customer or ERP selects Send, Correct or Cancel under SPEC-SEI-023 entry actions. Correct creates a separately numbered rectifying invoice referencing the original, then enters normal sending at step 1. Cancel checks the existing submission's eligibility and uses its original target and destination. A later rejection or other update can prompt a new action choice; it does not automatically start cancellation or rectification.

Check connected access points — Send: the ERP discovers the customer's connected platforms and their qualified sending and receiving availability before offering a sender selection. SPEC-SEI-023 OUT-00 owns this check; SPEC-SEI-024 §2.0 assesses reuse of the onboarding API. A listed connection does not by itself establish readiness or activate a route. These sending checks also apply to a new rectifying invoice.

Choose sender platform / Indicate recipient platform: the customer or ERP explicitly supplies both choices for each invoice. The sender platform must be connected, ready and permitted for sending; it cannot default from NIF or onboarding. The recipient platform can be the same or different. A different destination requires a qualified delivery path, not sender onboarding to that recipient platform. SPEC-SEI-023 OUT-00/10 owns these checks and permits recipient-platform omission only for qualified resolution; an unresolved destination holds sending. One invoice has one recipient-delivery route without fan-out. Private exchange has a separate faithful public-copy action; original exchange through SPFE has no extra copy. The diagram shows the proposed Spain selection behaviour; API and route support still need qualification. REF-LOGICAL; INT-SND02; SPFE-S02 Articles 3.4/4.

Choose sending certificate — proposed: where the route requires a certificate, the sender can choose any eligible certificate, including one different from onboarding. Final readiness checks its current validity, acceptance for the selected platform and purpose, and authority for the represented business under SPEC-SEI-001 CERT-04/05. Per-send selection support remains to be qualified; transport authentication and invoice signing remain separate purposes.
Full-size SVG · Editable Draw.io · PNG.

Read the selected action from top to bottom. Send and Correct use steps 1–6 and the existing sending routes. Cancel retains its earlier submission context; it does not choose a new sending route. E marks blocked or uncertain sending work under SPEC-SEI-023 — Exceptions, errors and recovery. Cancellation's own branch shows denied and unknown-result recovery.

SPEC-SEI-023 cancellation eligibility owns the state and reason rules, including full customer rejection. SPEC-SEI-047 cancellation and rectification mapping explains the different API and SPFE paths. Cancellation and rectification remain independent.

Workflow boundary: the submission branches end at each sending action's recorded result. The cancellation branch ends at its evidenced outcome or owned recovery. Dashed recipient-access boxes show the destination context only: the same private platform, another private platform, or access through SPFE. Private platform B's retrieval of an original UBL invoice from SPFE is a proposed handoff, not a qualified implementation. SPEC-SEI-024 §2.2 owns route qualification; SPEC-SEI-026 file-role scenarios distinguish original retrieval from faithful-copy retrieval. Detailed receiving and lifecycle reporting retain their owning specifications.

Final candidates and qualified already-issued invoices still need current authority, final validation and an eligible route. A failed, stale or ambiguous lookup does not prove that no private address has been communicated to the sender by the recipient. Dispatch holds until the approved Spain rule and evidence resolve the destination. The public route for a customer who has communicated no private address remains a Source conflict for Product and Spain Compliance; the public-by-default rule reported in local guidance also conflicts with the proposed hold after a successful no-match when the customer had supplied a private address. See SPEC-SEI-023 OUT-09 and SPEC-SEI-043 section 2.

The ERP owns issuance. In Phase 2, the selected private platform sends the required faithful UBL copy to SPFE using its own capability; Sage observes the copy result reported by that platform. When Sage operates as the private platform, Sage sends the copy. A public connection is needed only for public recipient delivery, not for the Phase 2 copy. This platform capability is an Assumption: expected, not confirmed; the user-supplied PPIFE_competitor_analysis.xlsx marks SPFE integration as pending and is not preserved in this repository. How the private platform reports copy results and errors to Sage, and who retries a failed copy, remain a Gap. The local explorer mock illustrates SERES sending the copy to SPFE; it is illustrative, not implementation evidence. The ERP still makes one sending request, and recipient delivery and public-copy results stay independent. Technical success does not establish buyer acceptance. OUT-SPFE-R01; SPFE-S02 Article 4; OUT-13–15.

PDF responsibility: the local product generates the transitional readable PDF where the product rule applies. Send it to the recipient, never to the public platform. A qualified private attachment path may carry it; the public structured-invoice route needs a separate recipient PDF channel. SEI023 defines behaviour; SEI024 assesses upload and delivery. RD238-T2.
SEI023 retains the process and activity order, exception and recovery decisions, Spain rules and scenario checks. Recovery preserves successful actions and resolves only affected work.

tr.td: Shared design patterns
Retain revision binding, independent action results, approval evidence and recovery. Reusing these patterns does not prove existing code coverage.
FR sending APIs

Reuse the documented create/upload/event/detail flow as the baseline. The preserved OpenAPI snapshot is version 1.0.0; the guide is separate supplied evidence. Neither establishes Spain field support or the complete draft-to-issuance journey. INT-SND01/02; SPEC-SEI-024.
Shared capability with country binding
Qualify identity, addresses, document/profile selection, route evidence, trust and status mappings for the selected Spain route.
Transformation
Existing DTS is the preferred candidate. Qualify its build, Spain mappings, rule packs, semantic preservation and operations under SPEC-SEI-008. REF-DTS.
Spain-specific behaviour
Public recipient fallback, faithful copies and legal correction rules stay in Spain policy. Public transport and format evidence do not establish a ready Sage integration. SPFE-S02/S08/S16.
Unknown implementation
Preparation/final handoffs, copy/issuance coordination, per-action results, approval and portfolio coverage need named owners and evidence before activation.
Service-assisted draft entry and validation — TBC
ERP Product, API and Architecture must confirm the scope, owner and draft-to-final handoff before enabling this path.
OUT-Q01 Approval policy
Product, Identity and Spain Compliance must qualify eligible roles, manual/automatic decisions and revision binding. Missing evidence holds the dependent action.
SND-G09 Onboarding route handoff

The product direction allows per-invoice choice among ready, permitted sender connections. Implementation qualification remains open: selected-build support, connection/address coexistence and ownership constraints, public readiness and onboarding companion alignment. SPEC-SEI-023 SND-G09 owns the boundary and accountable roles.
Public-route rule

Open / Proposed + Source conflict: Product, Engineering and Spain Compliance must confirm the six OUT-09 cases, the conflict with local public-by-default guidance, accepted evidence and the lookup retry window.
OUT-Q03 Issuance and private-platform copy

ERP, E-Invoice and Spain Compliance owners must prove the issuance/copy boundary and partial/lost-result recovery. Private-platform copy capability is an Assumption; Integration/API owners must define copy-result/error reporting to Sage and failed-copy retry ownership. A saved queue intent alone is insufficient.
es.nif and withdrawal

Proposed: es.nif. Open: API, Routing and Spain Compliance must confirm routing-address semantics and NIE handling. Withdrawal via FP-SEI-002 is Open; FP-SEI-002 assesses a separate Global API command and approves no call here.
FR contract and Spain coverage

API and Integration owners must pin the preserved OpenAPI snapshot and deployed build, resolve its confirmed schema defects, and qualify country fields, representation support, idempotency and event meanings. Existing France fields do not establish Spain activation.
Transitional PDF delivery channel

Local Product, API, Integration and Compliance must qualify attachment or separate-channel recipient delivery. The existing attachment API is a reuse candidate; actual Spain support and delivery proof remain open under SND-G08.
OUT-Q02 Portfolio and accounting handoff
Separate optional scope; not required for the main single-invoice journey. Qualify it before enabling it.

ac:layout-cell.p: The business can see a separate known result or owned pending/unknown state for each action. An escalation or notification alone cannot close the invoice journey. Functional acceptance is in SPEC-SEI-023; engineering qualification is in SPEC-SEI-024. These drafts do not establish production readiness.
